# Fairpractice Injury Liens (`fairpractice-injury-liens`)

Tracks personal injury liens and letters of protection: open balances by attorney, settled cases not paid, dropped cases with balances, filing windows passed or near (from the years you set), open cases with no signed letter, reductions over your limit and cases with no recent update. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Injury Liens never contacts attorneys. Fairpractice Injury Liens never accepts or offers reductions.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-injury-liens demo
npx -y fairpractice-injury-liens mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: made-up patients, cases and law firms. Any likeness to real people or firms is chance.

- [`lien-cases.csv`](fixtures/lien-cases.csv). Planted:
  - L1: settled September 20 and still unpaid (8,000).
  - L2: the 2-year window set for TX ends December 1, with no suit recorded.
  - L3: an open case with 4,500 billed and no letter of protection.
  - L4: settled with a 40% reduction, above the 33% limit.
  - L5: no update since June 1.
  - L6: dropped with 3,000 open.
  - L7: the 3-year window set for NY ended May 1 with no suit recorded.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): filing windows of 2 years by default and 3 for NY. These are example numbers, not legal advice. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `liens_check` | List settled cases not paid, dropped cases, filing windows, missing letters, large reductions and stale cases, with open balances by attorney. | runs |
| `liens_write_report` | Write liens.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and liens.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/liens). | runs |
| `liens_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `liens_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `liens_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `liens_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `attorney_email_send` | Fairpractice Injury Liens never contacts attorneys. | refused |
| `reduction_accept` | Fairpractice Injury Liens never accepts or offers reductions. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `liens_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `cases` (required) | Lien or letter-of-protection log under --root: patient, case, attorney, injury date, state, LOP signed, charges, paid, reduction %, status, settled date, last update, suit filed |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: statute_years, warn_days, pay_days, stale_days, max_reduction_pct |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-injury-liens inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Lien cases (`cases`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `case_id` | text | Case, Case #, Case ID, Case Number, Claim #, File #, Matter |
| `attorney` | text | Attorney, Law Firm, Firm, Attorney Name, Counsel, Lawyer |
| `injury_date` | date | Injury Date, Date of Injury, DOI, Accident Date, Date of Loss, DOL |
| `state` | text | State, Venue, Jurisdiction, Case State |
| `lop_signed` | date | LOP Signed, LOP Date, Lien Signed, Letter of Protection, Lien Date |
| `charges` | amount | Charges, Billed, Total Charges, Lien Amount, Amount Billed |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Amount Paid, Payments, Collected, Received |
| `reduction_pct` | number | Reduction %, Reduction, Reduction Pct, Discount %, Write Down % |
| `status` | text | Status, Case Status, Stage |
| `settled_date` | date | Settled Date, Settlement Date, Closed Date, Resolved, Date Closed |
| `last_update` | date | Last Update, Last Contact, Updated, Last Status Date, Last Follow Up |
| `suit_filed` | text | Suit Filed, Lawsuit Filed, Filed, Litigation |

## Settings file (`liens_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `statute_years` | Filing window in years by state code, plus "default". You set these; Fairpractice Injury Liens does not know any state's law |
| `warn_days` | Days before the window ends to warn; default 60 |
| `pay_days` | Days after settlement to expect payment; default 30 |
| `stale_days` | Days without an update before a case is stale; default 90 |
| `max_reduction_pct` | Largest reduction your policy allows without sign-off; default 33 |

## Memory

`liens_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `liens_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-injury-liens": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-injury-liens",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-injury-liens -- npx -y fairpractice-injury-liens mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-injury-liens tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-injury-liens sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-injury-liens inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-injury-liens call liens_check '{"cases":"<cases>"}'
fairpractice-injury-liens eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-injury-liens demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
